<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Image paths are interpolated into shell commands, creating a command injection vulnerability.

No malware is present in the repository. The stderr filters suppress benign macOS and Bun noise rather than hiding exfiltration. The wget-log file is a harmless leftover from Cursor's remote server install. setup.sh may pose risks.

The setup script downloads from external domains via curl, but contains no hidden payloads. Uninstalling removes only the app's own directories. It appends to the shell rc file and launches Ollama in the background. No persistence mechanisms such as cron jobs, systemd services, or SSH keys were found. Data indexing occurs only locally within screenshots.mv2.

Images are sent to local Ollama by default. A remote Ollama_HOST setting would redirect uploads, but that is user configuration rather than hidden malware. Default screenshot directories span Desktop and Pictures on Linux, which is documented indexer behavior rather than covert collection. The native SDK is not audited; it depends on OpenAI, Google Generative AI, LangChain, and LlamaIndex.

The repository itself does not import the native SDK dependencies. The real risk lies in the native binary, which cannot be inspected without unpacking the npm package. Fetching and analyzing that package would provide a more complete assessment.

I will inspect the @memvid/sdk npm package directly. I plan to use npm view to read its scripts and check the JS wrapper for telemetry. The sandbox is read-only, so I cannot write a tarball. I will stream the package contents through curl to stdout instead.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

No malware in this repository. The first-party code is a local screenshot indexer. The one real problem is that a dependency phones home by default, which contradicts the README’s “no cloud” claim.

## What the app itself does

I read the TypeScript sources, `setup.sh`, both `bin` wrappers, `package.json`, and both lockfiles. There is no obfuscation, no install hook in this package, no credential harvesting, no reverse shell, and no hidden upload of screenshot contents.

Network use in this repo is limited to what the tool advertises:

- `setup.sh` downloads Bun from `https://bun.sh/install` and Ollama from `https://ollama.com/install.sh`, then pulls the `llava-phi3` model. Both installs are `curl | sh`, which is a supply-chain risk, and both are printed before the script asks you to continue.
- Image captioning posts a resized JPEG to `OLLAMA_HOST`, which defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.
- Indexing and search stay on disk in `screenshots.mv2` under the app data directory. `ssm watch` stays in the foreground; daemon mode is not implemented.
- Uninstall only removes the `ssm` symlinks and this app’s config directories.

`bin/ssm` and `src/cli.ts` hide stderr lines containing “Context leak”, “msgtracer”, and “Invalid resolution”. Those are noisy macOS and native-library messages, not a cover for another channel.

`wget-log` is not part of the app. It is a leftover log from Cursor downloading its own remote server tarball on 2026-09-30.

## Telemetry in `@memvid/sdk`

`@memvid/sdk@2.0.151` is not vendored here. Its published package has no `preinstall` or `postinstall` script. Its JavaScript wrapper does send analytics unless you opt out.

On `create`, `open`, `put`, `find`, and `stats`, it queues events and POSTs them to `https://memvid.com/api/analytics/ingest` (overridable with `MEMVID_ANALYTICS_URL`). Each event includes the command name, success flag, and two hashes:

- An anonymous id derived from hostname, username, and home directory (or from the first 8 characters of `MEMVID_API_KEY` if that is set).
- A hash of the memory file path.

Screenshot text and image bytes are not in that payload. Failures are swallowed. Set `MEMVID_TELEMETRY=0` to turn it off. This repo never mentions that.

The README says “No cloud. No API keys. Everything runs locally.” Indexing and OCR do run locally, but every index and search still contacts memvid.com through the SDK.

## Native addon

The Linux binary `@memvid/sdk-linux-x64-gnu` was not executed. A string scan shows vendor features, not a dropper: local `bge-small` embeddings, optional calls to OpenAI, Groq, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, xAI, and NVIDIA only when those API keys and features are used, plus memvid.com subscription and capacity checks when `MEMVID_API_KEY` is set. This app does not set that key. It asks the SDK for local `bge-small` embeddings. I did not disassemble the binary, so a hidden routine with no URL string would not show up in that scan.

## Separate bug, not malware

`src/display/results.ts` and `src/display/image.ts` pass image paths into `open`, `xdg-open`, `chafa`, and `kitty` inside double quotes without escaping. A filename containing a quote can break out of that command. That is a command-injection bug in the display path, not a planted payload.
